blocks.text: Structural disorders of nervous system result from abnormalities or damage to the physical structure of nervous system. Examples include brain tumour, and spinal cord injuries.

A brain tumor is an abnormal growth or mass of cells in brain. Brain tumors can be benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous). Brain tumour can arise from glial cells or from the neurons themselves. Causes: The exact cause of brain tumors is unknown, but risk factors include exposure to radiation, family history, and certain genetic mutations. Symptoms depend on the location of tumour. These may include headaches, severe nerve pain, paralysis, seizures, and coma. Treatment: Common treatments include surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.
